title: Domain Trust Relationship Created Or Modified
detection_hypothesis: If the authentication boundary is altered, the Security log on a domain controller will record one of the trust lifecycle audit events.

field_semantics.EventID: Numeric identifier of the Windows event record.

collection_prerequisites: The relevant advanced audit policy subcategory is enabled for success events.
Domain controller Security logs are forwarded for directory-scoped events.
expected_collection_gaps: Events raised on a domain controller that is not forwarding logs are invisible.
Security log wrapping on busy controllers can drop events before forwarding.
normalization_assumptions: EventID is an integer and Channel is the literal string Security.
Account names are provided without the domain prefix in TargetUserName.
ingestion_differences: Some pipelines rename EventID to event.code or similar.
Directory attribute events may arrive with XML-encoded values.
retention_considerations: Security log volume varies widely; 180 to 365 days is common for identity events.
false_positive_strategy: Trust changes are rare and always planned in a healthy environment. Treat every match as reviewable and correlate with the migration project record rather than excluding events.
tuning_guidance: Do not exclude trust events. If a migration produces repeated events, suppress only for the duration of the documented migration window.
test_strategy: Positive cases create and modify a trust. Negative cases cover a group change, a logon, and a policy change on the same controller.

attack_techniques.name: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification: Trust Modification

unmapped_defensive_objects_reason: No Detection Strategy, Analytic, or Data Component identifier for this technique was present in the pinned ATT&CK extraction used by this lab. Defensive arrays are left empty rather than populated with unverified identifiers. Unmapped techniques: T1484.002.
